chunks.label: Seeing friends again
chunks.rationale: Greet a friend warmly after time apart and apologize for going quiet.
chunks.interference: Aitakatta (I missed you, on meeting) versus aitai (I want to see you, while apart).

chunks.label: Inviting and finding a time
chunks.rationale: Ask if someone is free, invite them along or over, and fit around their schedule.
chunks.interference: Issho ni kuru? (come with me) versus issho ni ikanai? (shall we go together?).

chunks.label: Saying yes to plans
chunks.rationale: Accept an invitation, join in, and lock the plan in.
chunks.interference: Tsukiau also means 'to date', so 'X to tsukiau' isn't 'go along with X'.

chunks.label: Turning down nicely
chunks.rationale: Say no to plans without sounding cold.
chunks.interference: Kyou wa pasu is fine with friends but too blunt with a boss; use ikitai n desu kedo... there.

chunks.label: End of the night
chunks.rationale: Wrap up an evening out: thanks, getting everyone home, checking in later.
chunks.interference: Okuru means both 'see someone home' and 'send'.

chunks.label: Apologies and owning up
chunks.rationale: Apologize to a friend, admit a slip, and wave off someone's thanks.
chunks.interference: Warui ne (thanks, sorry to trouble you) versus warukatta (it was my fault).

chunks.label: Checking you follow
chunks.rationale: Catch up when you lose the thread and check you understood.
chunks.interference: Atteru? (is that right?) and aiteru? (are you free?) sound close.
members: ごめん、聞いてなかった

chunks.label: Remembering out loud
chunks.rationale: Show how sure your memory is as you talk.
chunks.interference: Tashika (if I remember right) versus tashika ni (true, good point).

chunks.label: Finding the word
chunks.rationale: Keep talking when a word won't come.
chunks.interference: Nante iu n dakke (what's the word?) versus nan dakke (what was it?).

chunks.label: Sharing news
chunks.rationale: Open a piece of news or gossip and build suspense.
chunks.interference: Shitteta? (did you know before?) versus shitteru? (do you know it?).

chunks.label: Moving a story along
chunks.rationale: Keep a story going, give the reason, and urge the speaker on.
chunks.interference: Sore de sa (and then) versus sore ga sa (but here's the twist).

chunks.label: Wrapping up a story
chunks.rationale: Sum up, finish a story, and handle the punchline question.
chunks.interference: Ochi nai (no punchline) sounds like ochinai (doesn't fall).

chunks.label: Leading in with kedo
chunks.rationale: Signal what's coming: a serious talk, a tangent, a long story, a small complaint.
chunks.interference: Hanashi modoru (go back to the topic) versus hanashi kawaru (change the subject).
members: ちょっと話があるんだけど
それで思い出したけど

chunks.label: Feeling low
chunks.rationale: Say you're down, stuck, fed up or unmotivated.
chunks.interference: Ochikonderu (down after a setback) versus nayanderu (stuck on a worry or choice).

chunks.label: Comforting a friend
chunks.rationale: Notice a friend is low, offer to listen, and ease their worries.
chunks.interference: Ki no sei (it isn't real) versus ki ni shisugi (you're worrying too much).

chunks.label: Warm reactions
chunks.rationale: React to something soothing, moving, flattering or kind.
chunks.interference: Tereru (shy at praise) versus hazukashii (embarrassed, ashamed).

chunks.label: Names and casual speech
chunks.rationale: Settle names and how casually to talk when you meet someone.
chunks.interference: None.

chunks.label: Telling friends to stop
chunks.rationale: Push back on teasing, nagging, old habits and spoilers.
chunks.interference: Uzai is far harsher than the others; recognise it before using it.

chunks.label: Teasing back
chunks.rationale: Rib a friend who's bragging or being silly.
chunks.interference: Baka ja nai no and choushi ni noru na turn insulting with a cold tone or with anyone you're not close to.

chunks.label: Jokes and group mood
chunks.rationale: Talk about jokes landing or flopping and who's spoiling the mood.
chunks.interference: Uso uso (just kidding) versus uso! (no way!).
